To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the language control system in the brain is shared between language comprehension and production, and that the language control mechanism is used in comprehension to select the correct language and meaning of words.

activation of the left inferior frontal gyrus and the anterior cingulate cortex in bilingual language comprehension depends on both the degree of cross-linguistically shared form and meaning of words and the composition of the stimulus list.
bilinguals activate the language control network when reading words that differ in cross-lingual form and meaning overlap.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the language control system in language processing.
the cognitive and neural processes that support bilingual word recognition
the question of how bilinguals manage their two language systems and how the brain supports this management process.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the language control system is activated in both language production and comprehension, and is not specific to language production.

the activation of the language-control network in bilingual language production and language comprehension is due to a shared control mechanism that allows bilinguals to efficiently and quickly process language.
the language control system is a network of brain areas that is involved in language processing in general and not only in language production.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

language control in bilinguals is a two-way street: language control is not only required to produce words but also to comprehend words in a context-sensitive manner. (PsycINFO Database Record (c) 2019 APA, all rights reserved)
the brain is a very flexible and adaptive system that can recruit different areas of the brain for the same task, depending on the context and the demands of the task.
the language control system is a shared resource that is used in both language production and comprehension, to ensure efficient and context-appropriate language processing.
The main takeaway from our work is that
bilingualism is a dynamic process that involves a constant interplay between language control and language comprehension.

the language control mechanisms identified for bilingual language production also operate in bilingual language comprehension, and that they are recruited to support control operations that are required for the rapid and efficient comprehension of language in the face of cross-linguistics ambiguity.
the language control system is not limited to language production but also plays a role in language comprehension.
